_what: Synthetic Dart accessor-scope and parameter-redeclaration gate for #3904 (DART-10, stacked on #3903 / DART-11), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution and bench/dart-deferred-imports: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, with ratios as the only timing gates. Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Dart ScopeResolver and pubspec loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a class or function misses an expected method CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. small = 64 units x 4, large = 256 x 4 (classes or functions 4x), dense = 64 x 16 (accessors per class or parameters per function 4x). accessors puts one class per file (lib/c<i>.dart, each importing lib/types.dart); params keeps every function in lib/main.dart. input_bytes is pinned per shape beside capture_groups and relationships and grows linearly in every size parameter (accessors 20763 -> 82935 large, 67611 dense; params 17968 -> 71692, 67120). Expected method edges per unit are computed from the source, not read back from the graph: each getter's local types `v.save()` as Address.save, each setter's `Other value` types `value.run()` as Other.run, `reader()` reads the untyped field and gets nothing; each `a<j>.run()` reaches Address.run because only the closure redeclares `a<j>`. On #3903's head the accessor form misses every setter edge and gains a wrong `reader -> Address.save` per class (32 missing and 16 wrong at 16 x 4), so this gate fails without #3904; the params form is identical there and measures the per-scope redeclaration count's cost.
_fingerprint_note: Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason/detail, file, name, position).
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_4n/t_n)/4: about 1 is linear, about 4 is quadratic. 1.5 (bench/scope-capture) on every ratio, including accessors_resolve_unit_scaling_ratio, which kept 2.2 while every class sat in one file (_one_file_note).
_one_file_note: Not gated: Dart resolution is super-linear in the number of classes in ONE file, and the term predates #3904. Fresh-process doubling sweep over 64 -> 1024 classes, three rounds, min of 3 after 1 warmup per cell: resolution 1.27 (1.21-1.33) with every class in lib/main.dart (`--shape crowded`) on main with #3904, against 0.98 (0.87-1.09) with one class per file (capture 1.12 vs 1.00); before #3904 (700443c9a) the one-file form measured 1.34 (1.27-1.42), with #3904 1.24 (1.16-1.33) in a separate sweep. A CPU profile at 256 vs 1024 classes in one file puts the growth in finalize: materializeBindings -> dartMergeBindings (languages/dart/merge-bindings.ts) grows x14.8 and findClassBindingInScope / lookupMatchingNameClaim (scope-resolution/scope/walkers.ts) x9. The gated accessors shapes therefore use one class per file; the one-file term is tracked in #3915.
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.
_negative_controls_note: Each a temporary edit, in the CI profile, with unchanged fingerprints. Rebuilding the workspace MRO once per parsed file (the Dart ScopeResolver buildMro hook in languages/dart/scope-resolver.ts; O(files x classes)) fails accessors_resolve_unit_scaling_ratio 1.901 > 1.5 (1.829 in a second run); under the earlier 2.2 budget it passed. Re-walking the scope body for every parameter binding in dartParameterRedeclared (O(parameters x body), languages/dart/captures.ts) fails params_capture_per_unit_scaling_ratio 1.672 > 1.5 on this tree (1.872 when first recorded). These are deliberate regressions, not baseline observations.

_measured_ci.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 25-80 on 15 cores)

_measured_full.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 25-80 on 15 cores)

_measured_note: Three CI-profile runs and one --full run of this runner on main with #3904 merged. Scalar ratios and millisecond values are per-metric maxima across the runs of that profile (rounded); the 57 s wall time is one run under load average ~80, the others took 15-17 s. peak_rss_mib (--full only) is each --shape child's high-water mark after one worker parse and one resolution, worker thread included; context, not gated. Exact shapes and fingerprints were identical in all runs; the accessors fingerprints changed from the one-file runner (file paths), the params fingerprints did not. The doubling sweeps in _one_file_note were measured separately with --shape --reps 3 --warmup 1 and are part of neither profile.
